title: Guaranteed tokens-per-minute commitment and remediation playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define a measurable, contract-ready SLA for dedicated customers expressed as a tokens-per-minute (TPM) throughput commitment, with a clear error-budget formulation, credit computation, and operational playbook that ties into autoscaler behavior and fleet controls.
background: Enterprise customers purchasing Dedicated pools frequently request a quantified throughput contract. Current SLA drafts describe aggregate throughput percentiles but lack a clear per-minute measurement, a defensible error-budget math, and guidance for how autoscaling and maintenance windows affect credits. This ticket consolidates a consumer-friendly TPM-based commitment, explains measurement, and proposes remediation language for contracts.
proposed_solution: 1) Define the SLA metric: 'Committed TPM' is the contractual minimum of sustained tokens processed per minute per committed GPU-equivalent resource over a daily rolling window. 2) Measurement windowing: compute per-minute TPM across customer routes and map to committed capacity. 3) Error budget: measure minutes where observed TPM < Committed TPM; error_budget = total_committed_minutes - failing_minutes. 4) Credits: proportional to token-deficit aggregated across the billing period, with caps and minimums. 5) Operational controls: autoscaler hysteresis and pre-warm rules to prevent false positives, maintenance exclusion windowing, and failover policies. 6) Contract language snippets for SOW and MSA.
measurement_spec: - Source: Redwood telemetry (metric: dedicated.pool.tpm.minute) emitted per AZ and pool. - Aggregation: compute observed_TPM for each minute as tokens_served / 1 minute. - Mapping: scale observed_TPM against customer's committed_TPM by applying committed_shares for multi-tenant reserved pools. - Window: 30-day rolling period used for credit calculation; day-level reporting for customers. - Handling missing telemetry: treat missing telemetry as failing minutes after 2-minute grace unless a maintenance flag is set.
error_budget_formula:
- committed_minutes = committed_TPM > 0 ? (committed_TPM_window_minutes) : 0
- failing_minutes = count of minutes where observed_TPM < (committed_TPM * (1 - degradation_tolerance))
- error_budget_remaining = committed_minutes - failing_minutes
Notes: degradation_tolerance defaults to 2% to account for measurement jitter. For example: monthly_committed_minutes = 30 * 24 * 60 * committed_shares_factor. If failing_minutes exceed threshold, customer is eligible for credits as defined below.
credit_computation:
- Token deficit per failing minute = max(0, committed_TPM - observed_TPM)
- Aggregate token_deficit = sum(token_deficit per failing minute) over billing period
- Credit_amount = min(credit_cap, (aggregate_token_deficit / committed_TPM) * committed_monthly_fee * credit_scale)
- Credit_scale default: 0.50 (i.e., customer receives up to 50% refund of proportional fee tied to deficit)
- Credit_cap: not more than 100% of monthly committed fee. - Rounding: credits reported to nearest dollar. - Example provided in contract appendix.
escalation_playbook: - Detection: Observability alerts when failing_minutes > 5% over rolling 60 minutes. - Initial response: Ops page initiated, on-call notified; immediate capacity shadow autoscale triggered if available. - Customer comms: automated status page update within 10 minutes; PM/SE outreach within 30 minutes for P1 customers. - Remediation: attempt transparent model fallback or spill to burst capacity if policy allows. - Postmortem & credit calculation: incident review within 5 business days; credit applied on next invoice with detailed breakdown.
autoscale_integration: - Autoscaler policy required behavior: prioritize sustained TPM (not just latency) when deciding scale decisions for Dedicated pools backing committed customers. - Hysteresis: require 3 consecutive minute-over-threshold measurements before scale-up; 15-minute cooldown before scale-down to avoid oscillation. - Pre-warm: for scheduled load windows, pre-warm targets can be set via API to guarantee capacity at start-of-window. - Interaction with credits: autoscaler actions that were prevented by policy (e.g., capacity unavailable) are reflected in incident notes but do not negate credit eligibility unless explicit capacity reservation product is purchased.
fleet_controls_and_maintenance: - Maintenance windows: customers receive a 72-hour notice for planned infra maintenance; minutes flagged as 'planned_maintenance' excluded from failing_minutes if maintenance end-to-end confirmation is present. - Drains and AZ failover: define 'drain-aware' scaling to migrate traffic; failover that causes sustained TPM drop qualifies for remediation unless failover followed documented DR policy. - Capacity allocation: a committed pool's share table must be immutable within the billing period except via mutually agreed change requests to avoid measurement ambiguity.
contract_language_snippets:
- Service Commitment: 'Redwood will maintain a sustained tokens-per-minute (TPM) throughput of at least {committed_TPM} per allocated commitment unit, measured per minute, 99.5% of the time over the billing month, excluding scheduled maintenance.'
- Error Budget & Credits: 'If Redwood fails to meet the Service Commitment, Customer will be eligible for service credits computed based on observed token deficit as described in Appendix A. Credits apply to the invoice for the period in which the failure occurred and are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy.'
- Exceptions: 'Credits will not apply where degradation is caused by Customer misconfiguration, BYO model performance, or third-party upstream outages.'
acceptance_criteria: - Measurement pipeline implemented end-to-end for dedicated.pool.tpm.minute and surfaced in Console. - Example credit calculations and two worked examples (steady underprovision and burst failure) added to contract appendix. - Autoscaler policy update deployed in staging that honors TPM-based scale metrics and hysteresis. - Legal approves contract snippets. - SE/Support runbook for incident handling and customer notification created.
decision_log: - 2026-02-18: Chose TPM/min metric vs. RPS because token counts directly map to cost and charging units. - 2026-02-25: Agreed on 30-day rolling window and 2% jitter tolerance after infra/observability sync. - 2026-03-03: Legal proposed limiting credit_scale to 0.5 by default; product accepted but will allow negotiable field for enterprise deals.
open_questions:
- Should we offer an optional 'burst-banking' add-on where customers can bank unused TPM minutes for future bursts? (pricing & accounting implications)
- Do we support per-route TPM commitments or only pool-level commitments for initial launch?
- How to reconcile multi-AZ partial failures when traffic is asymmetrically distributed?
